_note: ADR 0010 (T1-03) — fixed co-deployment battery, v2 (DECORRELATED). v1 was withdrawn: it contained problems that WERE the held-out transfer cases (Lotka-Volterra, Hopfield, Goodwin, GA), which stacks the positive pairs into the battery (a battery-authorship confound). v2 is GENERIC domain problems chosen NOT to coincide with the held-out transfers, so a held-out node-pair co-occurs only via genuine single-problem method-sharing. RESIDUAL CONFOUND (stated, not closed): the solver is the same model that has seen the held-out set — so this is a FAILURE-INFORMATIVE first read only (fail = trustworthy; pass = inconclusive, needs a model with no held-out exposure).

problems.problem: Heat is applied to one end of a metal rod. Describe how the temperature profile along the rod evolves toward its long-run shape.
A pole is balanced upright on a moving cart. Design a scheme that keeps it from falling over.
From a sample of 500 survey responses, estimate the population's average income and how confident you are in that estimate.
A courier must visit 12 cities once each and return home using the least total travel. Outline how to find a good route.
Two bodies orbit each other under gravity. Determine whether a given circular orbit is stable to small perturbations.
A single species grows in a habitat with limited food. Describe how its population size changes over time and where it settles.
A photograph is corrupted by random speckle noise. Describe how to recover a cleaner image.
Price a financial option whose payoff depends on an uncertain future asset price.
A reversible chemical reaction runs in a closed vessel. Find the concentrations it settles to.
On a social network, individuals adopt one of two opinions and update based on neighbors. What long-run patterns emerge?
Group thousands of patients into a few meaningful subtypes based on many measured features each.
Relate the pressure a gas exerts on its container to the motion of its molecules.
Design cruise control that holds a car at a set speed despite hills and wind.
Improve an enzyme's activity by choosing among many possible amino-acid changes under a limited experimental budget.
